text:
Oliver: FYI prod node g7b-12 just hit an OOM while serving a 55k-token long context. KV cache took the blame in the logs. Repro samples attached below.

Maria: ugh. any obvious spike in batch size or prefix reuse?

Oliver: not a batch spike, throughput steady. Profiling shows a slow drift: live KV working set grows ~20MB/min for long conversations until the slab runs out. Attached heap dump excerpt:
```
KVCache::allocated = 14.1GB
KVCache::resident = 13.9GB
slabpool_free = 32MB
paging_events = 412 in last 10m
page_eviction_failures = 6
OOM_trigger = kv_alloc(128MB) failed at 0x7fc...
```

Sam: paging_events that high + eviction failures means eviction policy is thrashing. Are anchors (prefix pins) holding hot entries?

Oliver: yes, we see anchored prefixes from long-dialog sessions pinned with reuse_score > 0.9. Evicter refuses to touch them, but there are many small fragments so contiguous slab allocation fails. Fragmentation > 78%.

Ria: interesting — so it's not pure leak, it's fragmentation + anchoring preventing coalescing. Do we have kernel selection interactions? e.g., quantized kernels increasing per-token KV size?

Oliver: good catch. On those nodes we recently rolled kernel v2 that packs KV entries slightly differently (adds 8-byte header per entry). For 200k entries that adds ~1.6MB, but the bigger issue is layout change prevents previously compacted blocks from being reused until next compaction.

Maria: timeline: when did kernel v2 rollout happen?

Oliver: rolled 3 days ago to 40% of Serving fleet. This OOM was on a 40% node.

Sam: any easy mitigation short-term? i) force compaction on nodes, ii) reduce reuse anchors TTL, iii) soft-fallback to smaller model or CPU path?

Oliver: attempted forced compaction via /admin/kv/compact on the host — compaction reduced fragmentation to ~42% and recovered ~1.8GB, but compaction is heavy and stalls latency for ~200ms per request that triggers it.

Ria: probably need more graceful approach: add backoff-based anchor decay (reduce reuse_score by 10% per minute under memory pressure) + allow evicter to preempt pinned prefixes when contiguous failure count > N. Also add a soft degrade route to fallback model-compact (smaller KV footprint) when slab_free < 64MB.

Maria: agree. Also add a temporary rollback of kernel v2 until we validate layout impact. Can we toggle kernel selection per-deployment?

Oliver: yes, runtime supports kernel override via config flag. I've queued a rollback to the affected AZ, and flagged nodes for immediate compaction.

deploy-bot: deployment 3890010200: rolling kernel v1 back to pool-rust-az-a (20 nodes). ETA 12m.

Sam: follow-ups: 1) add observability metric for contiguous_free_runs and fragmentation ratio, 2) implement anchored-prefix decay heuristic, 3) add an emergency soft-fallback that routes long-context sessions to dedicated pool with larger slab sizes, 4) smoke test compaction latency impact on p99.

Ria: also add a unit test for kernel packing change so future kernel builds run a packing-compatibility compaction simulation.

Oliver: logging plan: dump a short trace when page_eviction_failures > 0 including top 20 anchored prefixes and their reuse_score + total entries. Will send a follow-up thread with logs.

Maria: thanks. Can someone own the postmortem action list?

Sam: I'll take the evicter heuristics + metrics.

Ria: I'll take kernel packing tests and rollout gating.

Oliver: I'll handle the immediate rollback and node compactions, and post the recovery timeline.

deploy-bot: alert: compaction tasks started on g7b-12. Node latency increased ~180ms for 2m, now stabilizing.

Maria: good catch everyone. Low noise channel: please keep ops updates here until we close the loop. :thumbsup:

Oliver: posting initial recovery summary in 30m.
